Autocorrelation of residuals within groups

Source: R/helpers.R
resid_acf.Rd

Computes the autocorrelation of model residuals within each trajectory, time series or other group, for lags from 0 to max_lag. At lag 1 it is the correlation between each residual and the residual one measurement earlier in the same group; lag 2 skips one measurement, and so on. Residuals are never paired across groups. Used in Advanced Statistics to check GAMMs for autocorrelated residuals; itsadug::acf_resid() does the same with base R graphics.

Usage

resid_acf(res, group, max_lag = 8)

Arguments

res

Residuals of a model, such as residuals(m).

group

The trajectory or series each residual belongs to, such as data$traj.

max_lag

The largest lag, in measurements.

Value

A tibble with one row per lag and the columns lag and acf. The autocorrelation at lag 0 is always 1. It is NA at lags as long as the groups, where there are too few pairs of residuals left.

Details

The residuals must be in the order of the data, sorted by time within each group, and res and group must have the same length: if the model dropped rows with missing values, drop them from group too.

Examples

library(simling)
# a straight line through the PRICE trajectories: the residuals of
# neighbouring measurements are strongly correlated
m <- lm(f2 ~ time, data = price_f2)
resid_acf(residuals(m), price_f2$traj)
#> # A tibble: 9 × 2
#>     lag   acf
#>   <int> <dbl>
#> 1     0 1    
#> 2     1 0.887
#> 3     2 0.647
#> 4     3 0.370
#> 5     4 0.164
#> 6     5 0.108
#> 7     6 0.178
#> 8     7 0.269
#> 9     8 0.307
